(hh)

To obtain leave, the father may file an affidavit no more than five
pages in length, double spaced, setting out the alleged changes in
circumstances.  The affidavit shall contain a statement as to what the father
now says his changed income is, and on what basis it has been calculated, with
reference to the marijuana business’ financial documentation.  The father shall
also file a fully completed sworn financial statement;

(ii)

The
father shall attach to his 14B Motion for leave, a copy of his personal income
tax return for the most recent tax year, and a copy of the business’ financial
statement for the most recent fiscal year end.  He shall attach any additional
documentation to which he makes reference in the affidavit, when setting out
what he now says his changed income is;

Declaratory
Relief Concerning the Cohabitation and Mortgage Agreement and Orders Concerning
the Property Terms in the Separation Agreement

(jj)

This
Court declares that the Cohabitation and Mortgage Agreement is not a genuine
document.  This Court shall not enforce the Cohabitation and Mortgage
Agreement;

(kk)

The father shall pay to the mother the sum of $250,000.00, plus
prejudgment interest set out below below, no later than 30 days after costs are
adjudicated in this case;

(ll)

After
costs are adjudicated in this case, but no later than 30 days thereafter, and
provided the money owing to the mother has been paid to her on account of
property and prejudgment interest, the mother shall transfer her interest in
the Thornhill Property to the father.  The father shall be responsible for the
cost of the preparation of the transfer;

(mm)

Concurrently with the transaction and payment, the father shall
discharge the mortgage to remove the mother from having any liability towards
the mortgage, or obtain a release from the lender of the mother’s obligations
under the mortgage.  The father shall be responsible for the cost of any
discharge or refinancing of the mortgage;

Orders
Pursuant to the Partition Act

(nn)

If the father fails to complete the property transaction set out above
by 30 days after costs are adjudicated, then the Thornhill Property shall be
sold;

(oo)

If the property is sold by agreement of the parties prior to costs being
adjudicated, the net proceeds of sale shall be held in trust until costs are
adjudicated;

(pp)

I shall remain seized of any further proceedings involving the sale of
the property and the distribution of the sale proceeds, if additional sale
terms are required;

Prejudgment Interest
Pursuant to the
Courts of Justice Act

(qq)

The father shall pay to the mother prejudgment interest in the amount of
$42,174.93;

(rr)

If either
party is of the view that there is a mathematical error in the calculation of
prejudgment interest in this Judgment, they may address that when costs are
dealt with.  This is not an opportunity to argue about the Court’s decision to
order prejudgment interest; just to address mathematical errors, if either
counsel sees such an error;

Confidentiality
and Costs Submissions

(ss)

The
Court has identified the parties and the child in this Judgment with initials;
[18]

(tt)

The
mother shall file costs submissions in writing, limited to five pages, double
spaced, plus a Bill of Costs and copies of any Offers to Settle.  Case law need
not be included but may be hyperlinked.  The mother may file further, brief
submissions, limited to no more than 2 pages,  double spaced, which may be
accompanied by any charts, to deal with the outstanding
section 7
expenses
issues and mathematical corrections to the Court’s prejudgment calculations, if
any.  The mother’s costs submissions shall be served and filed by October 22,
2025;

(uu)

The father shall file his written submissions on costs, and the
additional two matters referred to in the previous paragraphs (if any), by
November 24, 2025.  The father may file seven pages, double spaced, for his
costs, plus the additional two pages for the other matters.  The same
restrictions on attachments shall apply;

(vv)

The mother may file two pages of reply, double spaced, by December 8,
2025;

(ww)

If the Office of the Children’s Lawyer is seeking costs, then I may be
contacted and I will revise this schedule for the exchange of costs submissions;

(xx)

Costs will be dealt with in writing.  The Court reserves the right in
its sole discretion to invite oral submissions regarding costs and the other
two matters, once the Court reviews the written submissions;

(yy)

Any unpaid costs Orders made prior to the start of the trial, continue
to be due and payable, and need not be addressed in the costs submissions; and

(zz)

All other claims by either party are dismissed, except as set out in
this Order.  This includes both parties’ Notices of Motion and Cross-Motion to
amend his and her pleading, and the father’s 14B Motion dated July 3, 2025
concerning the same subject matter.

[5]

The father’s counsel did not object to the admissibility of these
photographs, although he would later object to the next batch of photographs
that the mother tried to introduce regarding the date of separation incident.

[6]

These photographs were included in documents books delivered prior
to trial, and no request for “metadata” had been made beforehand.

[7]

There was some confusion in the evidence about exactly how much
time the father had with L. after the December 2021 hole in the wall incident.
At one point the mother said orally during the trial that he had no parenting
time after the December 2021 hole in the wall incident.  The father said in his
trial affidavit that he had no uninterrupted time for an extended period.
During his examination-in-chief, he testified that he hadn’t seen L. in 2
months during this time frame.  In cross-examination, he agreed that he was
having day visits, but not overnights.

[8]

Although this petty dispute in the evidence about what was thrown
has absolutely no bearing on any decision I must make, the mother testified
that item of decor was an inexpensive piece of “chachka” made in Thailand, that
had been purchased from a discount store.

[9]

The mother informed the Court during her cross-examination, that
the father’s trial counsel in this family law case is also representing the father’s
sister in connection with that civil lawsuit.

[10]

The father’s first interruption occurred during the mother’s
counsel’s Opening Trial Statement.  The interruptions increased as the days
went on.  He even interrupted his own counsel.  The father was rude and
disruptive during Ms. Geraldo’s testimony.  He interrupted countless times.
Notably this occurred with some frequency during his own counsel’s cross-examination
of her, to the point that there was some bickering between the two.

[11]

On one occasion when I intervened, the father made a statement to
the Court and dramatically went to sit in the back of the court room (which is
not what I had instructed he had to do).

[12]

Incidentally, the Ontario Court of Appeal wrote that could be done
in
Martin v. 11037315 Canada Inc.
,
too:  see the last sentence of ¶ 20.

[13]

I find the mother’s evidence about the
extent of the email traffic that apparently exists about the Separation
Agreement to be relevant also, to whether anyone was exploited when negotiating
that document.

[14]

There were objections to questions about this, based on solicitor-client
privilege, and arguments about whether there was a limited, implied waiver of
privilege.

[15]

Counsel ought to have waited for re-examination, rather than trying
to intervene.

[16]

If steps have not been taken yet, it is not clear to me how exactly
he is going to appeal this, quite some time after the fact.   It also seems
that the proceedings resulting in his suspension resolved on consent, leading
me to query exactly how the father can appeal.  In any case, his ability to
appeal (or not) is neither here nor there for my purposes right now.

[17]

There are also positions taken for 2020 and 2021, but for the

and so I say nothing further about the mother’s analysis for 2020 and 2021.
